source_text: ἐφ' ὑμᾶς, καὶ μάθετε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ, ὅτι πρᾶός εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ.» Λήψεται τοίνυν τὴν τρυγόνα, φησὶν, «ὁ ἱερεὺς, καὶ ἀποκνίσει τῷ ὄνυχι. Σφάζεται γὰρ οὕτω τὰ ἐλαφρὰ τῶν στρουθίων. Πλὴν, οὐκ εἰσάπαν ἀποτεμεῖ, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τὴν κεφαλήν. Πέπρακται γὰρ οὕτως ὁ Χριστοῦ θάνατος, οὐκ εἰς μερισμὸν, ἀλλ' εἰς ἕνωσιν. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἐν ἀρχαῖς ἐπὶ τὸ Πάσχα τιθεὶς νόμον, καταθύεσθαι μὲν προστέταχε τὸν ἀμνὸν, πλὴν «Ἐν οἰκίᾳ βρωθήσεται,» φησὶ, «μιᾷ, καὶ οὐκ ἐξοίσετε τῶν κρεῶν αὐτοῦ ἔξω.» Μεμέρισται γὰρ οὐδαμῶς ὁ Χριστὸς, ἀλλ' εἷς ὁλοκλήρως καὶ ἐν ἑκάστῳ καὶ ἐν πᾶσίν ἐστι, καὶ αὐτός ἐστιν ἡ εἰρήνη ἡμῶν, συλλέγων ἡμᾶς εἰς ἕνωσιν τήν τε πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἐν ὁμοψυχίᾳ, καὶ τὴν δι' ἑαυτοῦ πρὸς Θεὸν ἐν Πνεύματι. Ὅτι τοίνυν οὐ μερισμοῦ πρόξενος, ἀλλ' ἑνώσεως πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὁ Χριστοῦ γέγονε θάνατος, ἐδήλου πλαγίως τὸ θύεσθαι μὲν τὸ στρουθίον, οὐ μὴν καὶ εἰσάπαν ἀποκείρεσθαι τοῦ σπονδούλου τὴν κεφαλήν· ὅτι δὲ ἁγιάζει τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν τῷ ἰδίῳ αἵματι, κατασημήνειεν ἂν, τὸ τῷ αἵματι τοῦ στρουθίου καταραίνεσθαι τὴν σκηνὴν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ. Μία δὲ τρυγὼν ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας, καὶ μία πάλιν, εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα, νοεῖται δὲ δι' ἀμφοῖν ὁ Χριστὸς, καὶ ἀποθνήσκων ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, καὶ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ὁλοκαυτούμενος τῷ Πατρὶ, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ἁπάντων ζωῆς ἑαυτὸν ἀνατιθείς. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ὑποβιβάζει γε μὴν ὁ νόμος καὶ εἰς τὸ λίαν εὐπόριστον τῆς θυσίας τὸν τρόπον· καὶ ἀναλόγως τοῖς ἑκάστου μέτροις ποιεῖσθαι προστάττει, τὸν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀρίστοις ὄκνον ὑποτεμνόμενος πανταχῆ, καὶ ἀπροφάσιστον καθιστὰς τοῖς ἑλοῦσι τὸ ῥᾴθυμον. Γράφει δὲ ὧδε πάλιν· «Ἐὰν δὲ μὴ εὑρίσκῃ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ζεῦγος τρυγόνων, ἢ δύο νεοσσοὺς περιστερῶν, καὶ οἴσει τὸ δῶρον αὐτοῦ, περὶ οὗ ἥμαρτε, τὸ δέκατον τοῦ οἶφι σεμιδάλεως περὶ ἁμαρτίας. Οὐκ ἐπιχεεῖ ἐπ' αὐτὸ ἔλαιον, οὐδὲ ἐπιθήσει ἐπ' αὐτῷ λίβανον, ὅτι περὶ ἁμαρτίας ἐστὶ, καὶ οἴσει αὐτὴν πρὸς τὸν ἱερέα, καὶ δραξάμενος ὁ ἱερεὺς ἀπ' αὐτῆς πλήρη τὴν δράκα αὐτοῦ, τὸ μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς ἐπιθήσει ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων Κυρίου, ἁμαρτία ἐστί. Καὶ ἐξιλάσεται περὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἱερεὺς, περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ, ἧς ἥμαρτεν ἀφ' ἑνὸς τούτων, καὶ ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ. Τὸ δὲ καταλειφθὲν ἔσται τῷ ἱερεῖ, ὡς θυσία τῆς σεμιδάλεως.» Ἀλλ' ἔν γε δὴ τούτοις, περὶ Χριστοῦ μὲν οὐκέτι, τὴν δὲ τοῦ προσάγοντος ζωὴν, καὶ τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ πρόσοδον, καὶ τὴν εἰς Θεὸν ἀφιέρωσιν, ὁ τῆς θυσίας ἡμῖν ὑποφαίνει τρόπος. Προσφέρεται μὲν γὰρ σεμίδαλις ἄρτου γένεσις. Ζωῆς δὲ τύπος, ὁ ἄρτος· ἀλλ' οὔτε λιβάνῳ καταπάττεσθαι δεῖν αὐτὴν, οὔτε μὴν ἐλαίῳ δεδεῦσθαι λέγει, σοφήν τε καὶ ἀναγκαίαν τοῦ τοιοῦδε τὴν ἀφορμὴν εὖ μάλα προαναφωνῶν, ὅτι περὶ ἁμαρτίας ἐστὶν, ἧς ἂν εἴη πάντη τε καὶ πάντως ἀπωτάτω τὸ ἱλαρὸν, ὡς ἐν ἐλαίῳ νοούμενον, καὶ μέν τοι τὸ εὐῶδες, ὡς ἐν λιβάνῳ τυχόν· εἴη δ' ἂν οὐκ ἀμφίλογον, ὅτι χρῆμα στυγνὸν καὶ ἄοσμον ἀληθῶς, ἡ ἐν ἡμῖν ἁμαρτία. Καταπλουτήσει δὲ ἐφ'
pass_a_gloss: [Matthew 11:29 continued from §12: ...upon you, and learn from me, for I am meek and lowly in heart.] So the priest, he says, will take the turtledove, and will nip it off with the fingernail (ὄνυξ). For in this way the light ones among birds are slaughtered. However, he will not cut off entirely, clearly the head. For in this way the death of Christ was accomplished, not for division (μερισμός) but for union (ἕνωσις). Therefore also at the beginning, laying down a law about the Passover, he ordered the lamb to be sacrificed, but [Exodus 12:46 quoted: in one house it will be eaten, and you will not carry any of its flesh outside]. For Christ has in no way been divided, but is one, wholly, both in each and in all, and he himself is our peace, gathering us into union, both that toward one another in oneness of soul (ὁμοψυχία), and that through himself toward God in the Spirit. So that the death of Christ became for us a bringer not of division but of union, the sacrificing of the bird showed indirectly, without its head being entirely shorn off from the neck bone; and that he sanctifies the Church with his own blood, the tent and the things in it being sprinkled with the blood of the bird would signify. And one turtledove is for sin, and one again for whole burnt offering; and through both Christ is understood, both dying for us, and being wholly burnt (ὁλοκαυτόω) to the Father for an odour of fragrance, and indeed dedicating himself as the price given in exchange (ἀντάλλαγμα) for the life of all. PALLADIUS: You spoke well. CYRIL: Indeed the law brings down the manner of the sacrifice even to what is very easily procured (εὐπόριστος); and it orders it to be done in proportion to the measures of each one, cutting away on every side hesitation (ὄκνος) about the best things, and making slackness without excuse for those who chose. And again he writes thus: [Leviticus 5:11-13 quoted: if his hand does not find a pair of turtledoves or two young of pigeons, he will bring his gift, concerning that in which he sinned, the tenth of the ephah of fine flour (σεμίδαλις) for sin. He will not pour oil upon it, nor put frankincense (λίβανος) upon it, because it is for sin; and he will bring it to the priest, and the priest, grasping from it his full handful, will put its memorial portion (μνημόσυνον) on the altar of the whole burnt offerings of the Lord; it is a sin offering. And the priest will make atonement for him concerning his sin which he sinned in one of these, and it will be forgiven him. And what is left will be the priest's, as a sacrifice of the fine flour.] But in these, no longer about Christ; rather the manner of the sacrifice hints to us at the life of the one who brings it, and the approach (πρόσοδος) in Christ, and the consecration (ἀφιέρωσις) to God. For fine flour is offered, the material of bread. And bread is a type of life; but he says it must neither be sprinkled with frankincense, nor moistened with oil, very well announcing beforehand the wise and necessary reason for such a thing, that it is for sin, from which cheerfulness (τὸ ἱλαρόν), understood as in the oil, would be farthest away in every way and altogether, and indeed fragrance, as perhaps in the frankincense. And it would not be disputable that sin in us is truly a gloomy (στυγνός) and scentless thing. But there will richly abound (καταπλουτέω) upon... [continues in §14]

Πλὴν οὐκ εἰσάπαν ἀποτεμεῖ 'will not cut off entirely', δῆλον ὅτι τὴν κεφαλήν. Πέπρακται (πράσσω) οὕτως ὁ Χριστοῦ θάνατος, οὐκ εἰς μερισμὸν ἀλλ' εἰς ἕνωσιν 'not for division but for union'. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἐν ἀρχαῖς ἐπὶ τὸ Πάσχα τιθεὶς νόμον, καταθύεσθαι προστέταχε τὸν ἀμνόν; Exod 12:46 LXX: Ἐν οἰκίᾳ μιᾷ βρωθήσεται, καὶ οὐκ ἐξοίσετε τῶν κρεῶν αὐτοῦ ἔξω. Ὅτι οὐ μερισμοῦ πρόξενος 'bringer of division' ἀλλ' ἑνώσεως πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὁ Χριστοῦ γέγονε θάνατος, ἐδήλου πλαγίως 'showed obliquely' τὸ θύεσθαι τὸ στρουθίον, οὐ μὴν εἰσάπαν ἀποκείρεσθαι τοῦ σπονδύλου τὴν κεφαλήν 'not entirely shorn off from the neck the head'. ὅτι ἁγιάζει τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν τῷ ἰδίῳ αἵματι, κατασημήνειεν ἂν 'would signify' τὸ τῷ αἵματι τοῦ στρουθίου καταραίνεσθαι τὴν σκηνὴν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ 'the tent and the things in it being sprinkled'. 'those who chose') τὸ ῥᾴθυμον. Quote Lev 5:11–13 LXX: ἐὰν μὴ εὑρίσκῃ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο νεοσσοὺς περιστερῶν, οἴσει τὸ δῶρον αὐτοῦ ... τὸ δέκατον τοῦ οἶφι (ephah) σεμιδάλεως (fine flour) περὶ ἁμαρτίας; οὐκ ἐπιχεεῖ ἔλαιον, οὐδὲ ἐπιθήσει λίβανον (frankincense), ὅτι περὶ ἁμαρτίας ἐστί; δραξάμενος πλήρη τὴν δράκα 'full handful', τὸ μνημόσυνον (memorial portion) ἐπιθήσει ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων Κυρίου; ἁμαρτία ἐστί; ἐξιλάσεται ... ἀφ' ἑνὸς τούτων ... ἀφεθήσεται; τὸ καταλειφθὲν ἔσται τῷ ἱερεῖ ὡς θυσία τῆς σεμιδάλεως. Ἀλλ' ἐν τούτοις περὶ Χριστοῦ μὲν οὐκέτι, τὴν δὲ τοῦ προσάγοντος ζωήν, καὶ τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ πρόσοδον (approach), καὶ τὴν εἰς Θεὸν ἀφιέρωσιν (consecration), ὁ τῆς θυσίας τρόπος ὑποφαίνει (hints at). Προσφέρεται σεμίδαλις, ἄρτου γένεσις 'origin/material of bread'. Ζωῆς τύπος ὁ ἄρτος. οὔτε λιβάνῳ καταπάττεσθαι (be sprinkled) δεῖν αὐτήν, οὔτε ἐλαίῳ δεδεῦσθαι (be moistened) λέγει, σοφὴν καὶ ἀναγκαίαν τὴν ἀφορμὴν (reason) προαναφωνῶν, ὅτι περὶ ἁμαρτίας ἐστίν, ἧς ἂν εἴη πάντῃ τε καὶ πάντως ἀπωτάτω (farthest away) τὸ ἱλαρόν (cheerfulness, gladness) ὡς ἐν ἐλαίῳ νοούμενον, καὶ τὸ εὐῶδες (fragrance) ὡς ἐν λιβάνῳ τυχόν 'perhaps'. οὐκ ἀμφίλογον 'not disputable' ὅτι χρῆμα στυγνὸν (gloomy) καὶ ἄοσμον (scentless) ἡ ἐν ἡμῖν ἁμαρτία. Καταπλουτήσει (καταπλουτέω 'be/make richly abundant') δὲ ἐφ' [continues in §14: ἑαυτῇ, τῆς ἀρετῆς ἀεί πως τὸ ἱλαρόν].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart’ (Matthew 11:29). The priest, then, it says, will take the turtledove and nip it with his fingernail (Leviticus 5:8), for that is how light birds are killed. Yet he will not cut it off completely; he clearly means the head. For so the death of Christ was accomplished, not for division but for union. That is why at the beginning, too, when he laid down the law for the Passover, he commanded that the lamb be sacrificed, and yet, he says, ‘It shall be eaten in one house, and you shall not carry any of its flesh outside’ (Exodus 12:46). For Christ is in no way divided (1 Corinthians 1:13); he is one, whole in each and in all. And he himself is our peace (Ephesians 2:14), gathering us into union, both with one another in oneness of soul and, through himself, with God in the Spirit (Ephesians 2:18). That the death of Christ has brought us not division but union, the bird showed indirectly by being sacrificed without its head being cut clean off the neck. And that he sanctifies the Church with his own blood (Hebrews 13:12) would be signified by the sprinkling of the tent and the things in it with the bird’s blood. One turtledove is for sin, and one, again, for a whole burnt offering; and through both Christ is understood, both dying for us and being offered to the Father as a whole burnt offering for a fragrant aroma (Ephesians 5:2), and offering himself up as the exchange for the life of all.

Cyril: The law, moreover, brings the form of the sacrifice down to something very easy to obtain, and commands that it be made in proportion to each person’s means. In this way it cuts away at every point any hesitation over the best offerings, and leaves those who choose slackness without excuse. Again it writes as follows: ‘If his hand cannot find a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, then he shall bring as his gift for the sin he committed a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, for sin. He shall not pour oil on it, nor put frankincense on it, because it is for sin. And he shall bring it to the priest, and the priest, taking from it a full handful, shall lay its memorial portion on the altar of the whole burnt offerings of the Lord; it is a sin offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed in any one of these, and it shall be forgiven him. And what is left shall belong to the priest, like the offering of fine flour’ (Leviticus 5:11–13). But in these provisions the manner of the sacrifice no longer points to Christ; it hints to us at the life of the one who offers, his approach in Christ, and his consecration to God. For fine flour is offered, the substance from which bread is made, and bread is a type of life. But the law says that it must not be sprinkled with frankincense, nor moistened with oil (Leviticus 5:11), and quite rightly it states beforehand the wise and necessary reason for this: that it is for sin. From sin, gladness, which is understood in the oil, would be utterly and in every way far removed, and so would fragrance, which is perhaps understood in the frankincense. It could not be disputed that the sin in us is truly a gloomy and scentless thing. But there will richly abound…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 15. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withdrawn English was not used for wording.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.

changes: 'pinch it off with his fingernail' -> 'nip it with his fingernail' (ἀποκνίσει with no object; 'it off' implied removing the whole bird)
'Yet he will not sever it completely, that is, the head' -> 'Yet he will not cut it off completely; he clearly means the head' (δῆλον δὲ ὅτι)
Exodus 12:46 lead-in: 'but: ‘It shall…’' -> 'and yet, he says, ‘It shall…’'
Restored 'And' before 'he himself is our peace' (καί)
'being offered whole to the Father as a fragrant aroma' -> 'being offered to the Father as a whole burnt offering for a fragrant aroma' (ὁλοκαυτούμενος)
'Again it writes this' -> 'Again it writes as follows'
Lev 5:11–13: 'the sin that he sinned' -> 'the sin he committed'
'his approach to God in Christ' -> 'his approach in Christ' (removed added 'to God'; τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ πρόσοδον)
'the stuff from which bread is made' -> 'the substance from which bread is made'
Modality: 'must be utterly … far removed' -> 'would be' (ἂν εἴη, potential optative); 'It is beyond dispute' -> 'It could not be disputed' (εἴη δ' ἂν οὐκ ἀμφίλογον)
'very well states' -> 'quite rightly it states' (εὖ μάλα προαναφωνῶν)
Fingernail clause checked in the PG 68 PDF transcription (col. 972): same text, quotation mark after φησίν unclosed; treating it as Cyril's paraphrase of Leviticus 5:8 is right
Checked: Matthew 11:29, Leviticus 5:8, Exodus 12:46, 1 Corinthians 1:13, Ephesians 2:14, Ephesians 2:18, Hebrews 13:12, Ephesians 5:2, Leviticus 5:11–13, Leviticus 5:11 all correct
Ending '…But there will richly abound…' joins §14 '…within itself the gladness of virtue…'
